paper.title: The Kite Experiment
paper.author: Benjamin Franklin
paper.edition: The Pennsylvania Gazette, 19 October 1752. Franklin’s complete six-paragraph statement only; later Priestley account and modern editorial introduction excluded.

rights: Public-domain original text and historical English edition. Source and edition records are kept outside the visible article.

blocks.en: As frequent Mention is made in the News Papers from Europe, of the Success of the Philadelphia Experiment for drawing the Electric Fire from Clouds by Means of pointed Rods of Iron erected on high Buildings, &c. it may be agreeable to the Curious to be inform’d, that the same Experiment has succeeded in Philadelphia, tho’ made in a different and more easy Manner, which any one may try, as follows.
blocks.zh: 欧洲的报纸经常提到费城实验的成功：在高大建筑物等处竖立带尖端的铁杆，从云中引出电火。好奇的读者或许愿意知道，同样的实验在费城也已成功，不过采用了不同而更简便的方法，任何人都可以按下面的方式尝试。

blocks.en: Make a small Cross of two light Strips of Cedar, the Arms so long as to reach to the four Corners of a large thin Silk Handkerchief when extended; tie the Corners of the Handkerchief to the Extremities of the Cross, so you have the Body of a Kite; which being properly accommodated with a Tail, Loop and String, will rise in the Air, like those made of Paper; but this being of Silk is fitter to bear the Wet and Wind of a Thunder Gust without tearing.
blocks.zh: 用两根轻巧的雪松木条做成一个小十字架，四臂的长度应使它们能抵达一块大而薄的丝手帕展开后的四角。把手帕四角绑在十字架的端部，就得到了风筝的主体。给它配上合适的尾巴、线环和绳子，它就会像纸风筝一样升到空中；但由于它用丝做成，更能经受雷雨阵风中的潮湿和风力而不被撕破。

blocks.en: To the Top of the upright Stick of the Cross is to be fixed a very sharp pointed Wire, rising a Foot or more above the Wood. To the End of the Twine, next the Hand, is to be tied a silk Ribbon, and where the Twine and the silk join, a Key may be fastened.
blocks.zh: 在十字架竖杆的顶端，固定一根非常尖的金属丝，使它高出木条一英尺或更多。在靠近手的一端，将一条丝带接在麻绳末端；麻绳与丝带相接的地方，可以系上一把钥匙。

blocks.en: This Kite is to be raised when a Thunder Gust appears to be coming on, and the Person who holds the String must stand within a Door, or Window, or under some Cover, so that the Silk Ribbon may not be wet; and Care must be taken that the Twine does not touch the Frame of the Door or Window.
blocks.zh: 当雷雨阵风似乎即将到来时，把风筝升起。握绳的人必须站在门内、窗内或某种遮蔽物下面，使丝带不会被淋湿；同时须注意，麻绳不能接触门框或窗框。

blocks.en: As soon as any of the Thunder Clouds come over the Kite, the pointed Wire will draw the Electric Fire from them, and the Kite, with all the Twine, will be electrified, and the loose Filaments of the Twine will stand out every Way, and be attracted by an approaching Finger. And when the Rain has wet the Kite and Twine, so that it can conduct the Electric Fire freely, you will find it stream out plentifully from the Key on the Approach of your Knuckle.
blocks.zh: 一旦有雷云来到风筝上方，尖端金属丝便会从云中引出电火；风筝和整根麻绳都会带电，麻绳上松散的纤维会向各个方向竖起，并被靠近的手指吸引。等到雨水把风筝和麻绳淋湿，使它们能够自由传导电火时，你会发现，当指关节靠近钥匙，电火便从钥匙上大量流出。

blocks.en: At this Key the Phial may be charg’d; and from Electric Fire thus obtain’d, Spirits may be kindled, and all the other Electric Experiments be perform’d, which are usually done by the Help of a rubbed Glass Globe or Tube; and thereby the Sameness of the Electric Matter with that of Lightning compleatly demonstrated.
blocks.zh: 在这把钥匙处，可以给莱顿瓶充电；用这样获得的电火，可以点燃酒精，并进行通常借助摩擦过的玻璃球或玻璃管所做的其他一切电学实验，从而完全证明这种电的物质与闪电的物质相同。
